Gradual narrowing over decades
Gradual narrowing is chronic atherosclerotic disease and produces claudication. Acute limb ischemia is a sudden occlusion.
Pain in calf muscles with walking
Exertional calf pain is intermittent claudication. Acute limb ischemia is abrupt occlusion with severe pain and absent pulses.
Swelling from blocked leg veins

Aortic dissection
Dissection arises from an intimal tear in the aorta, not from a foot ulcer. The listed ulcer complication is osteomyelitis.

It may be normal

Inner ankle above the heel

Front of the lower shin

Over 50% and life expectancy over 1 year

Over 70% and life expectancy over 2 years
Over 70% is the symptomatic threshold. Asymptomatic patients need over 80% and over 5 years' life expectancy.
Over 90% at any life expectancy

set1.q: What defines aortic dissection?
opts: A cavity outside the vessel wall
A cavity outside the wall is a pseudoaneurysm. Dissection is an intimal tear with a false lumen in the media.
Dilation of all three layers
Dilation of all three layers is a true aneurysm. Dissection separates the layers after an intimal tear.
Plaque narrowing of the lumen
Plaque narrowing is atherosclerotic stenosis. Dissection is an intimal tear creating a false lumen.
An intimal tear with a false lumen
Correct. Aortic dissection forms from an intimal tear typically contained by the media; the wall layers separate, creating a false lumen within the media where blood can pool.

The phrenic nerve serves the diaphragm. Groin pain reflects femoral nerve pressure.

Pulse rate, blood pressure, weight

Limb ischemia affects the feet. Ruptured aneurysm is often misdiagnosed as renal colic.
Peripheral neuropathy
Neuropathy causes burning feet. Rupture is often mistaken for renal colic or diverticulitis.
Renal colic
Correct. Ruptured aneurysm is often misdiagnosed as renal colic, diverticulitis, gastrointestinal hemorrhage or ischemic bowel, because the pain sits in the abdomen, back or flank.

Keratin is not an arterial wall protein. The failure is of elastin and collagen in the media.
Actin and myosin of the adventitia
Contractile proteins of the outer coat are not the named failure. Medial elastin and collagen fail.
Fibrin and platelets of the lumen
Fibrin and platelets make up clot and atheroemboli. Aneurysm reflects medial elastin and collagen failure.
Elastin and collagen of the media

Fatty core, thin fibrous shell

Small core, thick fibrous shell
A thick fibrous shell is the stable plaque. The vulnerable plaque is the one with a fatty core and a thin fibrous outer shell that can rupture.

Above the stenosis

set2.q: How is an ascending thoracic aortic aneurysm usually repaired?
opts: Open repair with root replacement
Correct. An ascending thoracic aneurysm often requires an open surgical approach with aortic root replacement, while a descending one can be repaired open or endovascularly.

Endovascular repair only

Medical therapy with no repair
Medical therapy alone does not fix a qualifying aneurysm. Ascending repair is usually open with root replacement.

set2.q: What does an endarterectomy do?
opts: Dissolves clot through a catheter
Dissolving clot is catheter-directed thrombolysis. Endarterectomy is open removal of plaque from inside the artery.
Removes plaque through open surgery
Correct. Endarterectomy is invasive surgery that removes plaque directly from inside the artery through an open incision; amputation is the last surgical option.
Dilates the artery with a balloon
Balloon dilation is angioplasty, an endovascular procedure. Endarterectomy removes plaque from inside the artery through open surgery.
Reroutes flow around the blockage
Rerouting flow with a vein or synthetic graft is bypass. Endarterectomy removes the plaque itself through an incision.
